title.en: Label playback of external solver data

summary: State the origin, units, time step and any resampling when a scene plays back results produced elsewhere.
objective: Keep the distinction between a simulation running in the scene and a recording of one that ran elsewhere.
applies_when: A field, deformation or flow animation comes from precomputed data.
Results were produced by another tool, dataset or offline run.
The scene invites parameter changes that the data cannot answer.
example_prompts: Play back the imported simulation with its metadata visible.
Show the flow results and be clear about what I can change.
negative_signals: Live solvers running in the scene, which have their own model disclosure.
Purely illustrative motion that makes no simulation claim.
not_for: Live solvers running in the scene, which have their own model disclosure.
Purely illustrative motion that makes no simulation claim.

principles: Playback and simulation look identical on screen and are epistemically different. A recording answers only the questions its run answered.
The metadata is the model: solver, mesh or grid, time step, units, physical parameters and the run configuration determine what the frames mean.
Resampling in time or space is a transformation of the data, and interpolated frames are inferred rather than computed, so smoothness can suggest resolution that never existed.

Controls must match authority, which is broader than selecting a stored run. Selecting among runs, interpolating between them and evaluating a fitted surrogate are all legitimate when each is labelled with its method and its support, and when the scene says where the underlying runs actually are. What misleads is a control that implies a solve nobody ran.
implementation: Carry the run metadata with the data and show it in the scene: source, solver, units, physical parameters, time step and spatial resolution.
Mark interpolated frames as interpolated, and state the interpolation method used between stored frames.

Classify each interactive parameter: selects a stored run, interpolates between stored runs, drives a labelled surrogate, or is fixed by the data. Show the parameter values actually covered so the viewer can see when a control is extrapolating.
Show the stored resolution honestly, for example by allowing the raw grid to be seen rather than only a smoothed render.
Distinguish derived quantities computed in the scene from quantities stored in the data.
observable_checks: Ask which parameter values the data covers; a scene that cannot answer is not carrying its metadata.
Step to a stored frame and to an interpolated one and confirm the scene distinguishes them.
Confirm displayed units and magnitudes match the source metadata rather than being rescaled for appearance.

Move each parameter control and confirm the scene says what it did: selected another run, interpolated between runs with a named method, evaluated a labelled surrogate, or refused with an explanation.

creative_affordances: Beautiful rendering of imported results is entirely legitimate and often the point.
An artistic interpretation of data is fine when it is presented as interpretation rather than as the result.
known_limits: Authored provenance guidance; it validates no dataset and asserts no simulation accuracy.
It does not prescribe a data format or a metadata schema.
